jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Financial Advisor Intern at Baystate Financial
jobs.description: Employer: Baystate Financial Expires: 10/18/2026 BEGIN YOUR FINANCIAL CAREER WITH AN INTERNSHIP WITH BAYSTATE FINANCIAL **We are currently interviewing for our Summer 2027 internship class in all of our New England offices** The first step in our interview process is to join a group information session via Zoom to learn more about Baystate Financial, the career of an advisor, and the industry in general. Our next information session is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20th at 11am. Please use the following link to register: https://financialguide.zoom.us/meeting/register/u6pqVizjStCHPfR_jwynsw In addition, please complete the Culture Index Survey listed below:https://go.cultureindex.com/p/3Cs6YkulwTG1 Baystate Financial is selecting full-time college students for our hands-on internship program. We are seeking highly motivated, entrepreneurial students, interested in a career in finance. Selected candidates will be given the opportunity to get fully licensed as a financial advisor, receive top-notch training and mentorship, and gain valuable professional experience transferable to any industry. Interns that prove to be an asset to the firm will be offered a full-time position upon graduating. About This Internship Right from the beginning students are given the resources needed to help clients achieve financial security. Financial Advisor Interns are taught how to build a financial services practice from the ground up. With the help of senior advisors and the Baystate team, students will meet with clients to learn more about their individual definition of financial security and develop a “financial roadmap” to get them from where they are currently, to where they want to be. At the end of the internship, successful interns will be able to exhibit: An Understanding of How to Create and Implement a Personal Financial Plan Client Acquisition and Marketing Strategies The Role of a Full Time Financial Advisor Exceptional Listening and Problem-Solving Skills The Ability to Work Well in Both a Team and Individual Capacity Candidate Characteristics Although there are a wide variety of college majors, personal backgrounds, and life experiences that will see success in this role, there are a few characteristics we see exhibited in the majority of our most successful interns: Strong Desire to Help People, Including Individuals, Families, and Small Businesses Motivated to Work in a Client Facing/ Sales/ Finance Role Competitive, with an Entrepreneurial Spirit and a Vision to Build and Grow Their Own Business High Standards or Integrity, Empathy, Competency, Work Ethic, and Professionalism “Interested individuals are invited to apply. And, while we appreciate every applicant's interest, only those under consideration will be contacted.” About Baystate Financial Since its founding in 1901, Baystate Financial has provided comprehensive financial services, life and disability insurance, estate planning, business succession planning, retirement funding, education funding strategies, and investment management to a diverse client base. More than a century of providing guidance, insight, and results has made Baystate Financial one of the oldest and largest wealth management firms in the northeast, with 12 offices in 6 New England States. Baystate Financial is comprised of a team of over 300 advisors and over 400 support staff, many of whom contribute to building financial plans for a wide variety of individuals and businesses. Baystate Financials’ strategy is tailored to help fulfill their client’s individual goals, with the understanding that every client’s goals are different.

jobs.title: Summer Games Data Scientist Intern - Charleston, SC at Booz Allen Hamilton Inc
jobs.description: Employer: Booz Allen Hamilton Inc Expires: 10/18/2026 University - 2027 Summer Games Data Scientist Intern - Charleston, SCThe Opportunity:The Summer Games is an innovative internship program that attracts some of the nation’s best and brightest students. The goal is to develop a breakthrough idea or solution for one of our customer's most pressing, complex, and multidimensional problems while developing valuable technical skills. This competitive and collaborative program attracts thousands of applicants each year. Simulating a real-world startup accelerator environment, the interns are divided into teams, each working on a different challenge project. Throughout the Games, interns receive mentorship from senior leaders, solve problems using Booz Allen’s products and unique engagement models, and leverage the power of collaboration in a team environment. The summer culminates with a final Challenge Cup competition and presentation to senior leadership. A past winner took the challenge of helping blind individuals navigate by using new technology and developing a business and market penetration plan. Teams have also helped to develop an app that gives military commanders an easy way to track real-time and open-source information about developing situations, including sudden attacks, fighting human trafficking, and even tracking the spread of a disease worldwide. Join us. The world can't wait. You Have: Experience with data exploration, data cleaning, data analysis, data visualization, or data mining Experience with statistical and general-purpose programming languages for data analysis Knowledge of structured and unstructured data sources Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in a Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field by Summer 2028 or Summer 2029 Nice If You Have: Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Possession of excellent critical thinking and analytical skills Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. CompensationAt Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $61,900.00 to $141,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. Identity StatementAs part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. Candidate AI Usage PolicyAI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided. Work ModelOur people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration, whether it occurs in person or virtually. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.Remote: If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.Hybrid: If this position is listed as hybrid, you will be expected to work from a Booz Allen facility frequently, in alignment with leadership expectations and the needs of the role. You may also be required to work from or visit a customer facility.Onsite: If this position is listed as onsite, work will primarily be performed at a Booz Allen office or customer facility, where employees will collaborate directly with colleagues and customers as required by the role. jobs.title: VESTER Campus Ambassador at Golden Hire Consulting
jobs.description: Employer: Golden Hire Consulting Expires: 10/18/2026 Join the Founding Team at VESTERYou buy a coffee at Starbucks. Instead of earning points, you earn Starbucks stock.That’s VESTER.VESTER powers stockback rewards — infrastructure that enables brands to reward customers with their own stock instead of traditional loyalty points.We’re growing quickly and hand-selecting some of the sharpest, most connected students on campus to help introduce VESTER to the next generation of investors and consumers.Why Join VESTER? Work Directly With the FoundersReceive direct mentorship from VESTER’s founding team, with experience spanning Société Générale, J.P. Morgan, and Goldman Sachs. There’s no middle layer — you’ll work closely with the people building the company. Get Paid for GrowthEarn compensation for every classmate you successfully sign up, with additional bonuses for reaching growth milestones.Learn Fintech, Markets & SalesGain hands-on exposure to how financial markets, fintech startups, customer acquisition, and enterprise sales operate before your first major internship. You’re active in clubs, Greek life, sports teams, student organizations, residence halls, or campus group chats.You’re curious. You’re interested in markets, investing, fintech, startups, or entrepreneurship. Prior experience is not required.You’re growth-minded. You take initiative, experiment with new ideas, and enjoy figuring out how to get people excited about something new.You’re an operator. You don’t wait around for instructions — you find opportunities and execute.You’re a student. Freshmen and sophomores are especially encouraged to apply, although juniors and seniors are welcome.What You’ll DoAs a VESTER Campus Ambassador, you’ll help grow VESTER within your university community by:Introducing students to VESTER and the concept of stockback rewardsDriving student sign-ups through your campus networkBuilding awareness through clubs, organizations, teams, and student communitiesTesting creative campus growth strategiesSharing feedback directly with VESTER’s founding teamHelping shape VESTER’s early campus growth strategyWhy Now?VESTER is only selecting a handful of ambassadors per campus.Joining now means getting involved at an early stage, working directly with the founding team, and helping shape how VESTER grows across universities.The strongest candidates will be considered first.

jobs.title: Business Intelligence Intern, Mission Critical at Ryan Companies
jobs.description: Employer: Ryan Companies Expires: 10/18/2026 Ryan Companies US, Inc. has an exciting career opportunity for a Business Intelligence Intern to join our National Mission Critical team! This is for a Summer 2027 internship for full-time undergraduate students with a graduation date December 2027 or later. The internship is a full-time, 40-hour week and will commence mid May 2027 and conclude before returning to school in August 2027. This is an in-office role with an expectation of 4 days in the office, 1 day work-from-home. The office location could be any number of current Ryan Companies locations: Minneapolis, Chicago, Dallas, Austin, Atlanta, or Tampa, for example. The Business Intelligence Intern, Mission Critical is the intersection of data analytics, process improvement, and innovation. This position will possess the proven ability to drive change using data insights, process engineering, and organizational collaboration and will work closely with project and sector leadership to proactively identify operational issues, diagnose root causes, and lead solutions through technology enhancements, process redesign, and effective change adoption. Some things you can expect to do: Process Improvement & InnovationEngage project teams to conduct root cause analysis to uncover underlying drivers of performance gaps, risk exposure, or execution delays.Design and implement solutions that may include changes to processes, tools, systems, or organizational structures.Monitor adoption and performance of implemented changes and adjust strategy based on feedback and measurable impact.Create documentation, SOPs, and training materials to support process standardization and scalability.Identify emerging and persistent data center industry challenges and collaborate with sector and other business leaders on deploying initiatives to address these Data AnalyticsIdentify and analyze operational inefficiencies across development, construction, and corporate functions using internal and external data sources.Translate findings into compelling insights using dashboards, visualizations, and executive-ready narratives with clear metrics and data-driven KPIs.Translate operational pain points into data requirements to identify collection opportunities with data engineering and field technology teams.Function as a bridge between data analytics, technology teams, and operational leadership to ensure integrated solution design. Some things you should expect to have:Pursuing bachelor’s / master’s degree in business, Engineering, Data Analytics, or related field.Proficiency in data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau), SQL, and analytics platforms.Effective communication, facilitation, and stakeholder engagement skills.Experience with project delivery, scheduling, or cost control tools (e.g., Procore, Smartsheet, Primavera) is a bonus.Compensation:The hourly base pay range is $20 - $25 per hour. The base rate may vary within the anticipated range based on factors such as the ultimate location of the position and the selected candidate's knowledge, skills, and abilities. Position may be eligible for additional compensation that may include commission and/or incentive program. Eligibility:Position requires verification of employment to work in the U.S. Benefits:Competitive SalaryMedical, Dental and Vision BenefitsRetirement and Savings BenefitsFlexible Spending and Health Savings AccountsLife InsuranceShort-Term and Long-Term DisabilityEducational AssistancePaid Time Off (PTO)Employee Assistance and Wellness ProgramsParenting BenefitsEmployee Discount ProgramsPet insuranceRyan Foundation – charitable matching fundsPaid Time for Volunteer Events Disclaimer: Eligibility may vary based on factors such as role, hours worked, employment status, length of service, location, and other considerations. Detailed information will be shared with eligible candidates during the hiring process, and the official terms and conditions will be outlined in each individual offer document. Ryan Companies is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Notice to Candidates:Please be advised that initial outreach regarding employment at Ryan Companies will only occur via email from the domain @ryancompanies.com email address. If you recieve communication from someone you believe is impersonating Ryan Companies, please report it to us at humanresources@ryancompanies.com Non-Solicitation Notice to Recruitment Agencies:Ryan Companies kindly requests that recruitment agencies and third-party recruiters do not submit unsolicited resumes or candidate information to any Ryan Companies employee or office. Ryan Companies will not be responsible for any fees or expenses associated with unsolicited submissions. If recruitment services are required, we will reach out directly to agencies on our approved vendor list. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation.

jobs.title: Maintenance Engineering Intern at APM Terminals
jobs.description: Employer: APM Terminals Expires: 10/18/2026 Job DescriptionWhat We Can OfferAt APM Terminals, we foster a dynamic learning and training culture that empowers our employees to excel. Our commitment to improvement means every team member has the opportunity to develop their skills and advance their careers by continuously refining how we work. Experience a diverse, multinational workplace where your operational insights directly influence how we work.Gain practical exposure to maintenance management, equipment reliability, and engineering support activities.Learn from experienced mechanics, storekeepers, and cross-functional operational teams.Participate in automation, system integration, continuous improvement, and safety initiatives.Develop technical and professional skills through hands-on experience in a large-scale port environment. Key ResponsibilitiesYou will support the maintenance and engineering teams while developing a practical understanding of terminal equipment and asset management processes. Under supervision, you may:Assist with maintenance management activities and initiatives that improve equipment and system performance.Support preventive maintenance processes, equipment inspections, troubleshooting activities, and safety practices.Help review and improve routine maintenance and repair checklists.Assist with data entry, maintenance shift reports, equipment records, and maintenance software updates.Apply basic mechanical, electrical, and automation principles while supporting daily operations.Participate in equipment troubleshooting efforts and help identify opportunities to reduce repetitive breakdowns and improve reliability.Contribute to continuous improvement projects, safety initiatives, and other assigned learning projects. Location: 2500 Navy Way, Terminal Island, CA 90731Additional InformationThis internship requires working both in office and operational environments. You may spend time indoors using computer systems and maintenance software, as well as outdoors supporting equipment-related activities and learning opportunities. This position is hourly, non-exempt, and is intended to provide valuable training and work experience for students pursuing academic studies. Determination on requests for reasonable accommodation are made on a case-by-case basis pursuant to an interactive dialogue between the applicant and the Company.

jobs.title: Sales Summer Internship at Packaging Corporation of America
jobs.description: Employer: Packaging Corporation of America Expires: 10/18/2026 As a Fortune 500 company, Packaging Corporation of America (PCA) is an ideas and solutions company. Our corrugated packaging business seeks to be the leader in helping our customers — large and small — package, transport and display products of all kinds. Our white paper business delivers Paper With Purpose by providing the highest level of customer service and operational excellence. We have approximately 15,000 team members in more than 100 locations in the United States that strive to meet the local needs of our customers. Our mission is to serve the needs of our customers, today and tomorrow, with products and services that exceed expectations for performance and environmental responsibility. People • Customers • Trust Program Overview: PCA’s 13-week (May – August) Sales Summer Internship offers hands-on experience across key departments of Design, Production, Customer Service, and Sales while building foundational sales knowledge. Interns will also participate in a corporate office visit in Lake Forest, IL to engage with marketing, meet with PCA leadership, and network with fellow summer interns. Upon successful completion of the program, interns may be offered a full-time position to begin after graduation into PCA’s GIFT Program (rotational sales development program). Principle Accountabilities include:Each intern will be paired with a mentor to guide their development throughout the summerWork on special projects assigned to assist each business function of Design, Customer Service, Production and Sales.Understand PCA’s business, industry, and sales processBuild core sales skills: communication, presentation, time management, problem-solving, and networkingAssist with customer communication: inquiries, new items, lead follow-up, and complaint resolutionBuild a prospect list and visit customers with experienced Sales RepresentativesPresent a final project to the management team and fellow interns Educational Requirements:Must be currently enrolled student majoring in Sales, Marketing, Business or related discipline and have completed their freshman year. A minimum grade point average of 3.0/4.0 is required Must be eligible to work in the US on a full-time basisAbilities/Skills:Strong written, verbal and interpersonal skills are essentialMust be comfortable engaging with mentors, team members and customersCandidate must display maturity and a high level of professionalismMust be able to handle multiple projects or customer inquiries simultaneouslyMust be able to travel. PCA is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Veterans/Disabled and other protected categories All Qualified applicants must submit their resume to careers.packagingcorp.com COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS Starting salary for position: $25.00 - $30.00 per hour determined by your academic year.Paid Holidays.Upon hire, an employee is automatically enrolled in the 401k plan. The plan offers both pre-tax and Roth contribution options along with employer provided matching contributions.Disclaimer: The Compensation and Benefits information in this posting represents PCA’s good faith and reasonable estimate of what it may pay for this position. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Pricing Associate (Reston, VA or Remote) at ICF
jobs.description: Employer: ICF Expires: 10/18/2026 ICF is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Pricing Associate Intern to join our Corporate Pricing Team. In this role, you’ll learn to develop accurate, compliant, and competitive pricing solutions that support ICF’s proposals and contribute to meaningful client outcomes. You will work with members of the pricing department, operations teams, capture managers, contracts, finance, and proposal professionals to analyze solicitation requirements, support and build pricing models, and help prepare cost and business proposals for federal, state, local, and commercial clients. Our summer internship is full-time for 10-weeks beginning in early June and ending in early August. Work may be hybrid from Reston, VA or performed from any U.S. location. At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance. This is a strong opportunity for a candidate who is interested in growing in pricing, finance, cost analysis, and government contracting. You’ll gain exposure to the full proposal lifecycle, learn from experienced pricing professionals, and build skills in financial analysis, compliance, collaboration, and business strategy. The successful candidate will bring strong analytical skills, intellectual curiosity, a collaborative mindset, and a commitment to accuracy and continuous improvement. Key Responsibilities Support the development of timely, accurate, and compliant cost and business proposals that help ICF compete effectively and deliver strong value to clients. Review requests for proposals and related documents to identify pricing requirements, evaluation criteria, submission instructions, compliance considerations, and key assumptions. Assist in building, maintaining, and quality-checking pricing models, including labor, other direct costs, travel, subcontractor costs, indirect rates, fees, and escalation assumptions. Collect, organize, and analyze cost inputs from operations, subcontractors, finance, contracts, and other stakeholders to support complete, clear, and defensible pricing submissions. Document pricing assumptions, methodologies, and supporting rationale so proposal teams and reviewers can easily understand how pricing aligns with the proposed technical approach. Participate in pricing strategy discussions, proposal reviews, color team reviews, and internal approval processes by preparing analyses and responding to reviewer feedback. Prepare financial analyses, scenario comparisons, and pricing summaries that help proposal teams evaluate competitiveness, profitability, and risk. Contribute ideas to improve pricing templates, tools, quality controls, and processes that support consistency, compliance, and efficiency across proposals. Basic Qualifications By start date at least 15 completed credit hours in Accounting, Data Analytics, Economics, Finance, Management, Supply Chain Management or related field. Preferred Qualifications Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including formulas, data organization, workbook review, and the ability to learn and work with detailed pricing models. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work accurately with financial, operational, and proposal data. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize assumptions, analyses, and recommendations for different audiences. Attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to follow structured processes and meet deadlines. Interest in cost estimation, pricing, financial analysis, business operations, government consulting, or government contracting.

jobs.description: Employer: Baystate Financial Expires: 10/18/2026 BEGIN YOUR FINANCIAL CAREER WITH AN INTERNSHIP WITH BAYSTATE FINANCIAL **We are currently interviewing for our Summer 2027 internship class in all of our New England offices** The first step in our interview process is to join a group information session via Zoom to learn more about Baystate Financial, the career of an advisor, and the industry in general. Our next information session is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20th at 11am. Please use the following link to register: https://financialguide.zoom.us/meeting/register/u6pqVizjStCHPfR_jwynsw In addition, please complete the Culture Index Survey listed below:https://go.cultureindex.com/p/3Cs6YkulwTG1 Baystate Financial is selecting full-time college students for our hands-on internship program. We are seeking highly motivated, entrepreneurial students, interested in a career in finance. Selected candidates will be given the opportunity to get fully licensed as a financial advisor, receive top-notch training and mentorship, and gain valuable professional experience transferable to any industry. Interns that prove to be an asset to the firm will be offered a full-time position upon graduating. About This Internship Right from the beginning students are given the resources needed to help clients achieve financial security. Financial Advisor Interns are taught how to build a financial services practice from the ground up. With the help of senior advisors and the Baystate team, students will meet with clients to learn more about their individual definition of financial security and develop a “financial roadmap” to get them from where they are currently, to where they want to be. And, while we appreciate every applicant's interest, only those under consideration will be contacted.” About Baystate Financial Since its founding in 1901, Baystate Financial has provided comprehensive financial services, life and disability insurance, estate planning, business succession planning, retirement funding, education funding strategies, and investment management to a diverse client base. More than a century of providing guidance, insight, and results has made Baystate Financial one of the oldest and largest wealth management firms in the northeast, with 12 offices in 6 New England States. Baystate Financial is comprised of a team of over 300 advisors and over 400 support staff, many of whom contribute to building financial plans for a wide variety of individuals and businesses. Baystate Financials’ strategy is tailored to help fulfill their client’s individual goals, with the understanding that every client’s goals are different.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Contracts Administration (Reston, VA) at ICF
jobs.description: Employer: ICF Expires: 10/18/2026 2027 Summer Intern, Contracts Administration At ICF, we work on projects that have an impact on real people. From ensuring families have a house that will survive the next hurricane, to helping curb teen vaping, to keeping our nation safe from cybersecurity threats, and more - ICFers are changemakers who do work with purpose. We are currently hiring interns to join our Contracts, Procurement and Pricing (CPP) teams (Contracts, Subcontracts, Purchasing, and Compliance). This group is part of the internal support process within ICF, helping the project teams win and manage their projects. We help shape policy and procedures to comply with government, commercial, state, and local practices to ensure we remain compliant with our client guidelines. Some of ICF’s major clients include Federal Highway Administration, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Exelon Utilities, LA Metro, Centers for Disease Control (CDC), Army Research Institute and Puerto Rico Dept of Housing. This is a full-time, 10-week, entry level internship position that begins in June and ends in August 2027. The internship will work a hybrid schedule from our Reston, VA office (2x per week). At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance. Pay is $23 per hour. As a Contracts Intern, you will provide direct support to the ICF Contract Administration (CA) Team by: Assisting with the review of Non-Disclosure and Teaming Agreements for future business opportunities where ICF will be a subcontractor. Assisting with the management of contract files on the Contracts’ SharePoint site (e.g., naming, reorganizing, uploading documents, identifying documents by type and tagging them). Assisting with contract set-ups in our Contract Management System. Assisting with internal data calls and internal audits. You will gain valuable experience in the proposal development process from the CA’s point of view to include: Reviewing solicitation terms and conditions (RFPs, etc.) Assisting with the business/price volume response to include: compliance review, writing the price narrative, and completing required forms/certifications. Coordination with the proposal response team, including Pricing, Subcontracts, Proposal Coordinators, et al., including attending formal proposal review meetings. As a Subcontracts Administration Intern, you will provide direct support to the Subcontracts Administration Team by: Assisting with the drafting of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Teaming Agreements, and modifications to existing agreements related to future business opportunities where ICF may engage companies or independent consultants as subcontractors or partners. Supporting vendor setup and maintaining subcontract records in SharePoint to help ensure the accuracy and completeness of subcontract compliance files. Using Microsoft Copilot and other approved productivity tools, as appropriate, to assist with summarizing solicitation or agreement requirements, organizing compliance information, and improving the efficiency and quality of administrative work products, subject to review and approval by the Subcontracts Administration Team. Assisting with the preparation of subcontractor Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Requests for Quotations (RFQs) for distribution to external vendors, consultants, or teaming partners. You will gain valuable experience in subcontract management and proposal development from the perspective of Subcontracts Administration, including: Reviewing Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and related solicitation documents to identify subcontract requirements, terms, and conditions. Coordinating with proposal response teams, including Pricing, Contracts, Proposal Coordinators, and other stakeholders, by attending formal proposal and subcontract review meetings. Supporting communications with potential and existing subcontractors regarding documentation, compliance requirements, and related administrative needs. As a Purchasing Intern, you will provide direct support to the ICF Purchasing Team by: Assisting with the review, drafting, and negotiation of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Master Services Agreements (MSAs), Software as a Service (SaaS) and other software subscription agreements, Statements of Work (SOWs), and Purchase Orders (POs). Supporting procurement file compliance activities, including preparing procurement award summaries, price analyses, and contract documentation. Conducting market and supplier research to support sourcing and procurement strategies. Serving as a liaison between suppliers and internal business units to address purchasing inquiries, explain purchasing processes, and assist with issue resolution. Assisting with supplier onboarding, contract administration, and procurement-related reporting and data analysis. Supporting internal spend analysis, data reconciliation, and process improvement initiatives. You will gain exposure to the sourcing and proposal process from a Buyer’s perspective, including: Preparing and distributing Requests for Proposal (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and Requests for Information (RFIs). Participating in supplier sourcing and competitive evaluation activities. Reviewing supplier proposals for completeness, responsiveness, and compliance with procurement requirements. Supporting supplier negotiations and contract award activities. Assisting with supplier performance and risk assessments. As a Compliance Intern, you will focus on supporting policy, reporting, and data analysis efforts that support the Contracts, Procurement, and Pricing team as well as other ICF stakeholders. Duties may include: Creating new AI bots and job aids for purchasing system compliance topics and contracts compliance guidance Researching state and local regulations and requirements for comparison with federal law Tracking and updating clause matrices for U.S. Government regulations Assisting in data analysis and reporting for small business utilization, prime contract data, etc. Individuals with a focus-area preference (Contracts, Subcontracts, Purchasing, and/or Compliance) should note such on their cover letter or resume, otherwise, applicants may be considered for any of the above teams. Basic Qualification: At least 30 credit hours of college coursework completed by start date. U.S. Citizenship is required per Federal contracts Preferred Qualifications: College studies in Accounting, Business Administration, Communications, Data Analysis, Economics, Management, Marketing, Psychology, Project Management, Public Policy, Supply Chain Management & Logistics or other related field. Interest in government contracting and procurement, research analysis, negotiating, business administration and government consulting. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills. Strong attention to detail. Strong communication skills (written/verbal). Strong computer skills (Microsoft).

Take the opportunity to gain insight into at least one other business area, paving the way for valuable future relationships.Work on real-world projects: Apply your skills on the job through business-driven projects to reinforce your learning and gain hands-on experience.Develop your skills through world-class training and support: Access Hilton University’s e-learning modules and business library while building knowledge through business-driven projects.Grow with personalised guidance: Benefit from regular feedback and coaching to ensure your progress is supported at every stage of the programme.Hilton Perks: Including our Go Hilton Team Member Travel Program, which provides you with access to heavily reduced hotel room rates for you, your family & friends. Salary & Benefits: £27,500 gross per annum & private healthcare. Location: At our EMEA Headquarters in Watford, with some flexibility depending on team and business need. You will benefit from a subsidised restaurant, a games area and a free in-house gym. Our Placement OpportunitiesWe have a range of placement opportunities within our highly talented Finance department:Hilton Finance Centre of Excellence:The Hilton Finance Centre of Excellence has two placement opportunities available, one in our Order-to-Cash (OTC) and another in our Record-To-Report (RTR) team. These placements provide exposure to a wide range of corporate finance activities, including journal postings, balance sheet reconciliations, VAT and revenue analysis, audit support, and financial reporting.Interns will work closely with experienced professionals across various finance functions within the Centre of Excellence, contributing to the monthly close process, supporting compliance and control activities, and engaging in continuous improvement initiatives. You’ll gain insight into Hilton’s financial systems and processes, develop your analytical and organisational skills, and build a strong foundation for a career in finance. This is a unique opportunity to be part of a collaborative, fast-paced team within one of the world’s most recognised hospitality brands, where innovation and excellence are at the heart of everything we do. Finance Global Brands & Commercial Services (GBCS) Placement:The GBCS Finance team supports Hilton’s Brand and Commercial engine - driving brand loyalty, top-line revenue and market share. This is a Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) arm of finance that is primarily responsible for the budgeting and forecasting of corporate expenditure across Brands, Sales, Marketing, Revenue Management and Technology functions.The team works with a wide range of stakeholders across multiple regions with varying reporting needs, so there are excellent opportunities to develop both analytical and business partnering skills. As an intern, you will support all aspects of our monthly deliverables and will have a unique opportunity to learn about our commercial operations, whilst getting to know the teams driving these initiatives. Statutory Reporting Placement:The UK Statutory Reporting and Accounting team is responsible for UK statutory reporting across Hilton’s international business, including preparation of all UK statutory accounts for audit, development of technical accounting judgments and estimates and compliance over other statutory requirements.Hilton has over 50 companies registered in the UK that between them report the results of UK leased hotels and international managed and franchised hotels. The team are responsible for the accurate and timely preparation of UK statutory accounts and related regulatory filings, ensuring full compliance with FRS101 and Companies Act requirements and meeting the filing deadline at Companies House. The team is also a critical business partner throughout the Finance organization, partnering closely with Tax, Treasury and Financial Planning & Analysis teams.As an intern, you will support the preparation and audit of statutory accounts under FRS 101. This includes preparing supporting workings, updating documents, and ensuring they agree to underlying records. This role provides the unusual opportunity to see the whole profit and loss account and balance sheet of a small group of hotels rather than one section of the balance sheet on a global basis. The role requires managing multiple tasks to help the team meet deadlines. What We’re Looking ForWe are seeking individuals who embody the Hilton Values in addition to the following criteria:A current bachelor’s or master’s student completing a degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Economics, or other equivalent, that includes a required 12-month year in industry placement.Availability to begin full-time employment on 5th July 2027, for a full-time 12-month placement.You must have the independent right to work in the UK for the full duration of the 12-month placement. Please note that this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route, so we are unable to consider applications from candidates who would require sponsorship. If you hold a visa or status that allows you to work in the UK full-time without sponsorship (e.g. Settled Status, Pre-Settled Status, where a 12-month work placement is a permitted, required & assessed part of your UK University degree, or other independent work permissions), you are welcome to apply.Fluency in English (spoken and written).You should be able to demonstrate a genuine interest in Finance.You should be able to demonstrate a high level of numerical and analytical capability. Selection ProcessApplications are now open—don’t miss your chance to apply! Submissions close on Tuesday 20th October 2026Our selection process is designed to bring out your best and help us get to know you. It includes:Online assessments.In-person Assessment Centre at our EMEA Headquarters in Watford (26th November 2026). While the process is rigorous, it’s also the first step in your personal growth journey with Hilton. If selected, you’ll begin developing the skills, connections, and confidence to thrive in your career.To ensure every application receives fair consideration, invitations to the final-stage assessment centre will be issued after applications have closed. Please complete each stage promptly and keep an eye on your inbox for updates.We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing reasonable adjustments for applicants and employees with disabilities. If you require any support or adjustments during the recruitment process or to carry out the essential requirements of the role, please contact us.

jobs.description: Employer: Inner Peak Expires: 10/21/2026 Marketing Intern: B2B Growth & Digital PresenceInner Peak builds mental health support for students, and we sell it to K-12 districts and universities. The team is small. There is no marketing function yet, and that's why we are hiring you: you'd be building it next to our VP of Sales & Marketing, who you'd report to directly.Worth saying up front, we don't have a playbook to hand you. We're still writing it. Some of what you try is going to flop. That's ok. We are paying you to learn together with us. What goes out, how often, who we engage with, how fast the following growsDo the same for Instagram and TikTok, which are earlier and messierSet up and manage paid campaigns on LinkedIn, Meta, and Google. Great if you have, not a dealbreaker if you haven'tYou're fine with a plan made Tuesday looking different by ThursdayYou'd rather send us a rough draft on Monday than a perfect one in three weeksPay:$1,000 a month, plus 10% commission on any deal that closes from a lead marketing brought in. jobs.description: Employer: The Center for Arts & Innovation Expires: 10/21/2026 About Us:At The Center, we believe creativity is one of the most important human capacities we have. It is how we imagine what could be, ask better questions, solve problems, adapt to change, and create what comes next. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: C++ Software Developer Intern at Scalp Trade
jobs.description: Employer: Scalp Trade Expires: 10/21/2026 We are seeking a driven and intellectually curious C++ Software Developer Intern to join our dynamic trading firm. This is an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience building high-performance trading systems while contributing meaningfully to our operations. You will work closely with experienced engineers in a mentorship-rich environment, learning cutting-edge low-latency systems design, trading infrastructure, and modern C++ development practices. This internship is designed to accelerate your growth as a software engineer while you help develop tools and strategies that directly impact our trading operations. If you thrive on learning, enjoy solving complex technical problems, and want to understand how financial technology works at scale, this is the role for you. Key Responsibilities & Learning Objectives Develop and Optimize Components: Under mentor guidance, design and implement features for automated trading systems, with emphasis on understanding the 'why' behind architectural decisions in high-performance environments.Collaborative Development: Contribute to core trading platform enhancements alongside senior engineers, learning best practices for low-latency, distributed systems.Code Quality & Design: Learn and apply SOLID principles, modern C++ patterns, and system design concepts through hands-on code reviews and pair programming sessions.Performance Analysis: Participate in profiling and optimizing trading system components; understand tuning techniques for real-time operations.Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document code, design decisions, and lessons learned to build your technical communication skills.Problem-Solving: Work on well-scoped technical challenges that build your analytical and debugging skills in a production environment. Required Skills & QualificationsStrong Foundation in C++: Solid grasp of C++ fundamentals (STL, memory management, move semantics, templates). Production experience not required; demonstrated projects or coursework show readiness.Core CS Fundamentals: Comfortable with data structures, algorithms, and basic systems concepts (threading, process synchronization).Quick Learner: Able to rapidly pick up new tools, libraries, and frameworks with minimal guidance.Linux Familiarity: Comfortable working in Linux environments; shell scripting and command-line tools are a plus.Collaborative Mindset: Excellent communication skills; eager to learn from mentors and ask clarifying questions. Preferred Skills Multi-threading Experience: Practical familiarity with concurrent programming, thread safety, and synchronization primitives.Network Programming: Exposure to socket programming, TCP/IP, or distributed system basics.Additional Languages: Proficiency in Python, C#, or other systems languages broadens your perspective.Financial Markets Interest: Curiosity about trading, equities, options, or how financial markets work—we teach the rest.Database Exposure: Familiarity with SQL or understanding of how databases store and retrieve data at scale.Version Control & Tooling: Experience with Git, debugging tools (gdb, valgrind), or profilers (perf, flamegraph). Personal Attributes Intellectual Curiosity: Genuine interest in understanding how systems work, from code to infrastructure to business outcomes.Growth Mindset: Embrace challenges and feedback as opportunities to learn. We expect you to grow significantly over the internship.Ownership & Initiative: Proactive in seeking learning opportunities and taking on well-scoped responsibilities with minimal oversight.Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid changes; thriving in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.Collaborative Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills with a preference for brainstorming and learning from teammates.Passion for Technology: Excitement about staying current with modern C++ and high-performance systems. What You'll GainHands-On Production Experience: Work in a real, production trading environment—not a sandbox. Your code runs strategies that generate revenue.Mentorship from Experts: Learn directly from senior engineers with deep expertise in low-latency systems, C++, and financial technology.Comprehensive Technical Knowledge: Understand high-performance systems design, from kernel tuning to network stack optimization.Career Acceleration: Build a portfolio of impactful projects and establish relationships with leaders in fintech.Potential for Conversion: Strong performers are considered for full-time roles upon graduation or at the conclusion of the internship. Compensation: This internship is paid at $7,000 per month for the program.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Nonprofit Accelerator Internship at University Impact
jobs.description: Employer: University Impact Expires: 10/21/2026 Nonprofit Accelerator Internship – UI Charitable Outcomes Lab(Priority Applications Due 9.25.2026) BackgroundUI Charitable helps financial advisors and their clients give more impactfully. We work with ~1,300 families and ~400 financial advisors, and we manage $500+ million in charitable assets. More importantly, we have moved over $350 million out the door to nonprofits and impact investments working to improve the world's most pressing social and environmental issues. Why We Think This Work Matters NowTwo forces are about to reshape philanthropy. The AI boom is creating a new generation of wealth, and the founders and employees holding that ownership are deciding how to structure their giving. Most of them will want to move money out faster than the sector can absorb it. Over the same period, as much as $124 trillion will change hands through 2048, with an anticipated $18 trillion of it going to charity. We are building the infrastructure to turn that money into real improvements in people's lives. The Problem You Will Work on For This InternshipA lot of charitable dollars do not produce the lasting change donors expect. Plenty of funded organizations will never solve the problem they exist to solve, and money alone will not fix that. Most attempts to address this try to change donor behavior, including several of our own. So we are working on the organizations instead. What We Are BuildingEight years of building the infrastructure gives us a direct relationship with thousands of nonprofits our donors already fund. We want to help them become more effective. The closest analogy is a business accelerator for nonprofits, or a private equity operating team. We assess an organization across the core functions of a well-run business, run it through a cohort based program, and reassess later to see what moved. So far we have a literature review, a survey of 150 nonprofits, an analysis of our own data, and some first drafts of our curriculum and a way we will measure the success of the program. We will judge the program by whether those organizations actually improve, not by how many attend. The Eight Functions We want all organizations our donors give to, to have a sound understanding of their outcomes and impact. But in order to do that, you have to be running an effective/efficient organization. We are organizing the program around the functions that separate organizations that grow from organizations that stall. Each intern will own work across multiple of these functions.Fundraising and the growth engine. Treating donor development as a sales pipeline with stages, conversion rates, and follow-up. (Sales, Marketing, and Branding)AI adoption and operations. Where AI can take real work off a five-person staff. Marketing and branding. Making the case for support to people who have never heard of the organization.Board development and governance. What effective boards do, and how to get a board to do it.Program measurement and evaluation. Outputs, outcomes, and impact, and how small organizations can measure honestly without a research budget. (Public Health, Statistics, etc.)Finance, accounting, and internal controls. Who approves spending, who reconciles accounts, and what gets outsourced.Technology and data systems. CRM, donor records, and reporting that does not live in the executive director’s head.Talent and leadership capacity. Hiring, retention, and how a small team allocates the hours it has. Position OverviewWe are hiring two interns to help run a year-long pilot. You will work directly with Gary McHardy (a Rhodes Scholar based in South Africa) and Tanner Mills (Sr. Associate at UI Charitable). The team is small and the program is new, which means you will own real pieces of the work rather than support someone else’s. You will interview nonprofit CEOs, build the assessment instruments, write and deliver curriculum, and sit in on calls with the senior advisors guiding the program. Duties and Responsibilities:Design the curriculum. Build the workshop content, templates, and tools for your assigned functions, covering what the best organizations do and how a five-person staff can actually do it.Deliver it. Run webinars, cohort sessions, and office hours. You will be the one teaching, not just organizing.Drive results at the organizations. Work directly with participating nonprofits to implement what the curriculum covers. The goal is a CRM that exists, a pipeline that gets worked, a board that shows up.Interview nonprofit leaders. Run discovery calls, take structured notes, and turn what you hear into changes to the program.Analyze the data. Segment organizations by size, growth trend, and reported need using assessment results and public financials.Measure our own results and make adjustments. Track baseline and follow-up scores and report the delta honestly, including where we did not move the needle.The above list is not exhaustive; additional tasks will for sure be assigned as necessary. Required Skills/Abilities:Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication. You will be talking with nonprofit executives and delivering material they will read.Analytical Skills: Able to work with survey and financial data, draw conclusions, and present findings clearly and concisely.Project Management Skills: Able to handle several workstreams at once, prioritize, and hit deadlines without being chased.Comfort with Ambiguity: This program does not exist yet. You should be comfortable proposing an approach, testing it, and changing it when it fails.Team Coordination: Work very well with other people as a high output team. Deliver on what you’re responsible for AI Fluency: Regular use of AI tools for research, drafting, and analysis, with the judgment to check the output.Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to break a large, vague problem into pieces someone can actually work on.Humility and a Desire to Learn: A strong interest in understanding UI Charitable’s tools and programs and their role in achieving social impact.Integrity: Keep commitments, admit mistakes, maintain confidentiality where appropriate, and act in the organization’s best interests at all times. Education and Experience:Currently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor’s degree. Business, economics, statistics, public health, public policy, marketing, computer science and communications backgrounds all fit.Coursework, work experience, or genuine interest in at least one of the eight functions listed above. Tell us which one or two in your application.Proficiency with spreadsheets, survey tools, and standard office applications.Prior nonprofit experience is welcome but not required. Physical Requirements:Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer. The expectation is that candidates would be able to commit 20 hours per week, in person. How to ApplyEmail Tanner at tanner@uicharitable.org with your resume and a short note, under 250 words. Tell us which of the eight functions you would most want to own, why you want to work on this, and about anything you have produced, built, sold, raised, or automated. jobs.description: Employer: OpenGov Expires: 10/22/2026 OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Why OpenGov?A Mission That Matters.At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. OperationsThe Trade Support team, part of Operations, supports the operational aspects of trade processing, reconciliation, financing, and reporting for all products across global markets - equities, derivatives, bonds, foreign exchange, and futures. Interns will gain exposure to working with traders and counterparties to resolve trading matters and help provide accurate books and records for the firm on a daily and monthly basis. Strategic ImplementationThe Strategic Implementation team leads complex, cross-functional initiatives that support the growth of Point72's businesses, partnering with Strategy, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, and Technology. Interns will gain exposure to the end-to-end program cycle —coordinating meetings and deliverables, building project plans and timelines, documenting current state, conducting root cause analysis, and developing playbooks for key activities. StrategyThe Corporate Strategy team is a small, multidisciplinary group reporting to the Chief Operating Officer that identifies, designs, and executes value-creating cross-functional initiatives and engages in new business and special situations. Interns will gain exposure to strategic priorities by supporting analyses on operations, performing quantitative and qualitative research (competitive analysis, industry trends, market conditions), and providing project management support on key initiatives. Regulatory ReportingThe Regulatory Reporting team provides governance across all regulatory filings and obligations globally, including submissions to the SEC, CFTC, NFA, MAS, FCA, SFC, and Kanto Finance Bureau. Interns will gain exposure to filing preparation and submission, execute data reconciliations and exception investigations, partner with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Risk, Technology, and Trading, and help identify automation opportunities that improve accuracy and reduce manual effort. TreasuryThe Treasury team supports the firm's credit and treasury functions across Central Funding, Securities Lending, and Broker Relations—verifying and disputing margin calls, reporting on counterparty exposure, investing excess cash, and negotiating margin terms with prime brokers and derivative counterparts. Interns will gain hands-on exposure to a wide range of financial instruments across global markets while working alongside senior treasury professionals. Human CapitalThe Human Capital team serves as trusted business partners and advisors within the Point72 community, committed to driving a distinctive culture that values collaboration, innovation, and adaptive performance. Interns will gain exposure to day-to-day HR operations including onboarding, employee records, and benefits administration, along with recruiting and interview coordination, HR reporting and project work, and compliance and privacy best practices for handling confidential information. LegalThe Legal team works to deliver exceptional legal services in a manner that promotes the firm’s performance with the utmost integrity and supports all Point72 groups globally with practical advice on a variety of complex legal and regulatory matters in an ever-changing, dynamic environment. Interns will gain exposure to regulatory filings and obligations, drafting and updating firm policies, due diligence reviews, and industry best-in-class automation and data visualization tools that support the department. About Point72Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry's brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people's long-term growth. For more information, visit https://point72.com/.The annual base salary is $75,000 (USD) which will be prorated based on internship start and end date. Actual compensation offered to the successful candidate may vary from posted hiring based upon geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, among other things.

jobs.title: Summer Analyst Corporate and Leveraged Finance at Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
jobs.description: Employer: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank Expires: 10/22/2026 Summer Internship:Credit Agricole CIB hosts a 10-week internship. This internship provides students with the opportunity to obtain relevant professional experience, network with colleagues and senior employees, and learn about the investment banking (IB) industry. Our internship includes one structured week of technical and functional training, on the desk work, networking/educational events, and a formal evaluation process. Different events during the internship include an opening/closing event, speaker series, community engagement, and general networking opportunities. Interns are provided with relevant work and case study material to enhance their skillset and prepare for a future in IB. If you are interested in a career in investment banking, this is the internship for you! Department: Corporate and Leveraged Finance Americas Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (“CACIB”) is the corporate and investment banking arm of the Crédit Agricole Group. Based in New York, CACIB’s Corporate and Leveraged Finance Group (“CLF”) includes Corporate Origination Americas that originates, structures, and distributes syndicated loans and bilateral facilities for the Americas as well as The Leveraged, Acquisition and Telecom Finance Group (“LATFG”) originates leveraged finance solutions for financial sponsors and corporates through leveraged loans and high yield bonds.. Furthermore, the Group acts as a primary underwriter and is active in the secondary markets to provide liquidity to investors. CLF is seeking a student in their penultimate within interest in the Financial Industry. CLF provides a full array of financing solutions for corporate clients and financial sponsors. The team originates, structures and distributes investment grade and leveraged debt financings, including investment grade and leveraged loans, high yield bonds, and bridge financings across general corporate and various structured finance sectors. This person will provide support to both junior and senior bankers, assist in financial modeling and credit analysis, analyze corporate credit ratings, conduct market research, and provide general support across various projects. The role offers an opportunity to assist in all aspects of deal execution and become an integral part of Credit Agricole’s CLF franchise. The ideal candidate will demonstrate strong work ethic and initiative, excellent analytical and communication skills, superior organizational ability, and the capacity to work under pressure. An understanding of banking and capital markets would be preferred. The position offers exposure across various groups/platforms across the bank and the opportunity to see syndicated loan, Term Loan B and HY bond transactions executed from beginning to end. Prepare presentation materials including marketing information and internal reporting documents as well as the maintenance and updating of various data bases utilizing financial analysis skills. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Marketing & Growth Lead at Forbidden Well
jobs.description: Employer: Forbidden Well Expires: 10/22/2026 Marketing & Growth Lead (Paid Internship → Full-Time)Forbidden Well · New York, NY · Hybrid, 2 days a week on site$1,500/month · 90-day paid internship, designed to convert to full-time This is a six-figure job on the other side of 90 days.The internship pays $1,500/month. The full-time role it converts into starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and the revenue you generate. We built the path that way on purpose — we'd rather pay it out than not. You will own marketing. All of it.This is not an internship where you're handed a task list and asked to schedule someone else's posts. You will own the strategy, the calendar, the campaigns and the creative. The concepts are yours. The pitch ideas are yours. The call on what we run next is yours.We'll work alongside you to stay aligned on direction and make sure you have what you need, but you are not waiting on us to tell you what to do. If you need someone to hand you assignments, this is the wrong job. If you've been waiting for someone to hand you the keys instead, read on. You are the keeper of the brandForbidden Well should look and sound like one thing everywhere we show up: email campaigns, social posts, stories, the grid, and every other form of communication we put out. Someone should be able to see any piece of our content and know instantly that it's us.That means more than staying consistent. You'll continuously fine-tune that identity, stay organized in how we market, and be deliberate about what goes out and why. No random posting. Every piece has a purpose you can explain.You own every external relationshipThis role owns all points of contact with other spas, vendors, modeling agencies and brands — curating them, organizing them, and keeping them alive over time.A real example: a friend recently connected us to the owner of a very successful spa in Miami. We make the introduction, and from there it's yours to develop into something lucrative — a referral partnership where their clients coming to New York come to us, and ours heading to Miami go to them. First introduction to signed, working partnership, end to end. That's the job. What you'll runBrand, content and social across Instagram and TikTok: your concepts, your voice, your calendarBrand consistency across every channel we touch, and the standards that keep it that wayEmail marketing, including weekly campaigns and automated flowsPaid social and lead generation campaigns with our agency partnerPartnerships and outreach: spas, vendors, modeling agencies and like-minded brands, plus the co-marketing campaigns that come out of themPhoto and video shoots: concept, casting, scheduling and running the dayOur podcast, using our full in-house studio: booking guests, recording, editing and publishingLocal search, our Google Business Profile and our Google reviews programDaily and weekly reporting on what's working Who this is forYou generate ideas without being asked and can defend themYou write well and have taste. You can tell the difference between good and almost goodYou have an eye for consistency and it bothers you when something is off-brandYou're comfortable talking to people and turning an introduction into a relationship that lastsYou're comfortable with AI tools, especially Claude, and use them to move fasterYou're organized enough to run a shoot, a podcast taping and three campaigns in the same weekYou want to build something, not pad a resume Where it goesThis 90-day period is a prerequisite for a full-time, long-term role, and it's how we both find out if this is the right fit. We're hiring for the person who runs marketing at Forbidden Well for years — someone who grows as the company does and takes on more as we open more. If you hit the benchmarks, which we'll set with you and review together, the full-time role starts at $75,000 and can exceed $150,000 based on performance and revenue generated. About usForbidden Well is a luxury wellness house in New York built around IV therapy, advanced treatments and a client experience that feels like nothing else in the city.Apply with your resume and anything you've made that you're proud of: content, campaigns, a brand you built, a project that worked. Tell us about one brand whose identity you think is airtight and why, and one relationship or partnership you started and kept going. We care more about what you've shipped than where you've interned.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Spring 2027 Fundraising Intern at Partnership for Public Service
jobs.description: Employer: Partnership for Public Service Expires: 10/22/2026 Job DescriptionApplication Deadline is October 19.For Spring 2027, the Partnership will prioritize hiring interns from the following schools: Florida International University George Mason UniversityOhio State University – John Glenn College of Public Affairs and the Washington Academic Internship Program (WAIP)Syracuse University – Maxwell School of Public AffairsTrinity Washington University University of California schools – UCDC Washington Center ProgramUniversity of MarylandUniversity of Michigan University of Pennsylvania University of Texas at Austin – LBJ School of Public AffairsThis is a DC-based hybrid position. Interns must reside and have a permanent address in the Washington Metropolitan Region for the duration of their internship. ORGANIZATION The Partnership for Public Service is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization dedicated to building a better government and a stronger democracy. We believe that our future and our democracy depend on our ability to solve big problems—and that we need an effective federal government to do so. For 25 years, we have helped make this vision a reality by helping our government—the public institution most fundamental to our democracy—address current and future challenges.Our staff is diverse in experience and perspective, but at our core, we share a lot of the same traits. We are mission-driven, creative, collaborative, optimistic and inclusive.Our work is strategic, fast-paced and guided by our values:Passion for public service and our work toward a more effective government.People who promote a culture of learning, leadership, collaboration, inclusion and respect.Persistence to drive change, take strategic risks and deliver results.Promise to be trustworthy, nonpartisan and fiscally responsible.We hire smart and friendly people who are great at what they do and good to one another in the process. POSITION OVERVIEW The Partnership’s fundraising efforts extend across the organization and focus on ensuring long-term financial viability. The Development team identifies, cultivates and secures financial and in-kind support for the Partnership’s programs and activities. The Fundraising intern will learn the basics of nonprofit fundraising and relationship management, including how to conduct prospect research, cultivate new donors and work with our corporate sponsors and other existing supporters. Specific responsibilities may include identifying and researching prospective sponsorship, individual gift and foundation grant opportunities; drafting correspondence related to Partnership programs; providing support for internal and external meetings, including preparing, note-taking and observing; assisting with mailings or email invitation sends; and tracking donor interactions using our customer management system (Salesforce). jobs.title: Stanley A. Weiss Internship Winter/Spring 2027 at Business Executives for National Security
jobs.description: Employer: Business Executives for National Security Expires: 10/22/2026 The Stanley A. Weiss Internship program places high-performing candidates at the intersection of industry and national security. Interns work full time (40 hrs/week) to support Business Executives for National Security (BENS) in our mission to apply industry experience and best business practices to address the U.S.’s most pressing national security challenges. Interns will have the opportunity to contribute directly to BENS' three campaigns, each of which guide our work and partner engagement: Homeland Resilience and Response: The private sector plays an increasingly central role in protecting the American homeland. BENS brings business expertise to bear on national security challenges, working across domains and with key government partners to develop innovative public-private partnerships, secure critical infrastructure, improve domain awareness, respond to economic coercion, and foster energy resilience.Strengthening Supply Chains: The U.S. is overexposed to supply chain disruption. BENS is working to identify opportunities to strengthen U.S. and allied supply chains to build a more resilient national security industrial base. Current lines of effort include leveraging private sector insight to support state-level national security initiatives, scaling emerging technologies, and improving U.S. biosecurity.Mobilizing Private Capital: National security priorities increasingly depend on private investment to accelerate industrial capacity, finance the defense industrial base at scale, and modernize critical infrastructure. BENS connects private capital with these priorities by helping senior leaders think creatively about policies and tools to mobilize private investment, and by expanding the community of investors familiar with national security opportunities. Recognizing that threats to U.S. national security rarely stay within traditional borders, BENS also engages in programmatic work focused on broader geopolitical dynamics relevant to U.S. interests. BENS has long supported U.S. combatant commands and NATO strategic commands by examining business and economic conditions pertinent to their respective missions:Geopolitics and Economic Statecraft: BENS engages senior business and government leaders at the intersection of geopolitics and economic security. A signature element of this workstream is BENS' executive travel program, which brings private sector leaders to examine and offer insights on critical geopolitical issues. At the request of U.S. government partners and allies, BENS has sent delegations in recent years to Brussels, Athens, Hanoi, Buenos Aires, and Panama City.PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIESStanley A. Weiss Interns are essential members of the BENS team, contributing to the organization’s goals by working closely with government partners and BENS members within the national security community.Interns will:Gain subject matter expertise in a national security topic through in-depth research and presentations to BENS senior leadership.Track and analyze relevant policy developments focused on critical infrastructure, geopolitics and economic statecraft, the national security industrial base, and emerging technology. Support BENS staff in outreach and engagement with national security-focused government partners and business leaders. Assist with event preparation, including producing preparatory materials, supporting logistics, and working with event participants. Draft and edit pieces for the BENS Substack, external articles, member-led reports, and partner-facing memos.Attend, take notes on, and analyze Congressional hearings, external events, and key meetings with government and private sector stakeholders.Maintain and update membership databases.Set up and break down office events.Provide general administrative support. REQUIREMENTS Education and ExperienceCandidates are evaluated based on their skills and prior experience. Most successful applicants have recently completed, or are in the process of completing, an undergraduate or graduate degree. SkillsSelf-starting, entrepreneurial approach to work and a genuine curiosity to explore new subject areas and sectors. Strong research, writing, and organizational skills. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely to diverse audiences. Ability to manage multiple priorities and excel in a fast-paced environment. Exceptional interpersonal and professional skills, with the ability to engage confidently with senior business executives, military and government officials, and staff at partner organizations. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a team. Proficiency with standard office software and digital research tools.Candidates with prior coursework, research, or professional interest in areas such as critical infrastructure, economic security, private capital, emerging technologies, the defense industrial base, critical supply chains, and/or critical minerals are encouraged to apply, though this experience is not required. TERMThe spring internship will begin in the early January and end in mid-May. Interns are paid an hourly wage set at the current D.C. minimum wage and receive metro travel benefits. Interns are expected to work full time, though exceptions may be made for outstanding candidates with academic conflicts.TO APPLYTo apply, submit your resume and written responses through this form. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so early submission is encouraged. The final deadline to apply is Friday October 30 at 5:00 pm ET.
